DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 70 s. 2022 JUL 2 9 2022 Hon. ROSARIO M. DAPITON Punong Barangay Barangay Busao Maribojoc, Bohol Dear PB Dapiton: This has reference to your letter dated 4 April 2022 requesting for assistance and imploring the exercise of residual power of the Secretary to appoint someone to handle the hearing of an issue subject of Katarungang Pambarangay (KP) involving you as among the respondents, who also is the current chairman of the Lupong Tagapamayapa of the Barangay. Per your representation, you and most of the sangguniang barangay members in Barangay Busao signed a petition to remove sangguniang barangay member Elina Macalos as the president of Busao Centro Association, a private association. You represented that you signed the petition as members of the church in your private capacity and not as barangay officials. Also, you represented that sangguniang barangay member Macalos filed a case of Intriguing Against Honor before the Lupong Tagapamayapa against everyone who signed the said petition to remove her. According to you, there exists a conflict of interest in settling the dispute before the Lupon since you and some members of the lupon are respondents in the dispute. Hence, the request for assistance. We note at the outset that the chairman of the lupon who is also one of the parties to the dispute cannot preside in the mediation process in the katarungang pambarangay. However, the dispute herein may still be heard through mediation by the lupon or conciliation through the pangkat. A simple reading of Section 6, Rule IV, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules readily discloses that in the event the Punong Barangay ceases to hold office or is unable to perform its duties, said duties shall be performed by the officer succeeding the Punong Barangay pursuant to the rule on succession provided in RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC). Section 6, Rule IV, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules states: "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

"SECTION 6. Succession to or substitution for Punong Barangay. — In the event the Punong Barangay ceases to hold office or is unable to perform its duties enumerated in Section 1 of this Rule, the said duties shall be performed by the officer succeeding the Punong Barangay pursuant to the rule on succession provided in Section 44, 45 and 46, Chapter 2, Title II, Book I of Local Government Code of 1991". While, Section 1, Rule IV, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules provides: "SECTION I, Qualifications of membership. — To qualify for appointment to the Lupon, a person must have his actual residence or place in the barangay and must possess personal characteristics that indicate his suitability for the task of conciliation of disputes. Such suitability may be indicated by his integrity, impartiality. independence of mind sense of faimess. reputation for probity and other relevant considerations such as tact, patience, resourcefulness, flexibility and open-mindedness. Further, he must not be expressly disqualified by law from holding public office." (Emphasizing and underlining supplied) From the foregoing, a chairman of the lupon must always be impartial, independent of mind and with sense of faimess, and in the event that the said chairman is unable to perform its duties, the officer succeeding the punong barangay must perform the duties of the lupon chairman pursuant to the rule on succession provided in the LGC. We are of the view that the Punong Barangay (PB), who is the lupon chairman, becomes biased and loses the sense of fairness to hear the dispute before him/her once a he/she becomes a party to the dispute in the KP. Hence, once the PB becomes a party to a dispute in the KP, he/she cannot perform the duties of a mediation officer because of conflict of interests and prejudice. The PB then must inhibit or be substituted by the officer succeeding the PB. In this regard, we would like to inform you that since you are one of the parties in the dispute, you must be substituted as the chairman of the lupon by the highest ranking sanggunian barangay memberl, who must not be party to the dispute. Moreover, the dispute herein may be settled through the conciliation process or arbitration done by the Pangkat ng Tagapagkasundo (pangkat) once the mediation proceedings between the parties be rendered futile or were unsuccessful. The dispute then will be forwarded to the pangkat for conciliation or arbitration proceedings. Section 404 of the LGC specifically provides: Section 404. Pangkat ng Tagapagkasundo. — (a) There shall be constituted for each dispute brought before the lupon a conciliation anel to be known as the an kat n ta a a kasundo hereinafter referred to as the pangkatt consisting of three (3) members who shall be chosen by the parties to the dispute from the list of members of the lupon. 1 section 44 (b), R.A. 7160

Should the parties fail to agree on the pangkat membership, the same shall be determined by lots drawn by the lupon chairman. (b) The three (3) members constituting the pangkat shall elect from among themselves the chairman and the secretary. The secretary shall prepare the minutes of the pangkat proceedings and submit a copy duly attested to by the chairman to the lupon secretary and to the proper city or municipal court. He shall issue and cause to be served notices to the parties concerned. The lupon secretary shall issue certified true copies of any public record in his custody that is not by law otherwise declared confidential. (Emphasis ours) While Section 3 and 4 Rule V, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules provide: SECTION 3. Function. — All disputes not successfully settled by the Punong Barangay shall as far as possible be settled by the Pangkat through conciliation or arbitration. SECTION 4. Disqualification — A party may move to disqualify any member of the Pangkat by reason of relationship, bias, interest, or other similar grounds discovered after the constitution of the Pangkat. The Pangkat shall resolve the matter by majority vote. Its decision on this matter shall be final. From the foregoing, the parties may choose three (3) members of the lupon, who are not parties to the dispute, as their pangkat ng tagapagsundo to settle the matter through conciliation or arbitration or if the parties fail to agree on the pangkat membership, the lupon chairperson therein will determine three members by drawing lots to be distributed to members of pangkat. The parties may, however, move to disqualify any member of the pangkat by reasons mentioned above. In the matter at hand, if and when the mediation efforts or proceedings before the chairman of the lupon becomes unsuccessful, the parties should proceed to conciliation proceedings. If the parties do not reach an amicable settlement, the pangkat Secretary shall issue a certification to file action.2 The parties may, at any stage of the proceedings, agree in writing to have the matter in dispute decided by arbitration by the pangkat. In such case, arbitrational hearings shall follow the formal order of adjudicative trials.3 Also, it appears herein that not all the lupon members are party to the dispute. Thus, we are also of the view that the pangkat consisting of other members of the lupon who are not parties to the dispute shall be able to settle the matter promptly and fairly. Further, the appointment of someone who will handle the hearing of the dispute of the parties is unnecessary as it is not within the power of general supervision over the local governments of this Department4. 2 Section 4(f), Rule III, Katarungang Pambarangay Rules 3 Section 9, Rule VI, Katarungang pambarangay Rules 4 Section 5(a), Chapter 1, Title XII, Book IV of Executive Order No. 292

The Supreme Court, in the case of Taule V. Santos5, clarified the meaning of power of general supervision by the President through the Secretary of Local Government, viz: "Supervision means overseeing or the power or authority of an officer to see that the subordinate officers perform their duties. If the latter fails or neglects to fulfill them the former may take such action or step as prescribed by law to make them perform their duties. Xxxx The fundamental law permits the Chief Executive to wield no more authority than that of checking whether said local govemment or the officers thereof perform their duties as provided by statutory enactments. Hence, the President cannot interfere with local governments so Ionq as the same or its officers act within the scope of their authority." (Emphasis ours) Consequently, this Department cannot appoint someone to handle the hearing of the dispute since the we cannot interfere with the procedures of the Katarungang Pambarangay and we cannot interfere with local governments so long as the same act within the scope of their respective authority. Please be informed that the establishment and operation of the Katarungang Pambarangay or Barangay Justice System is mandated by Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse ary for Local Government OUSBA/MBD/LLLS-LRALLDnasm/rrao copy furnish: DIR. LEOCADIO T. TROVELA Regional Director.
